scope_change_reason: Pair-collision at draw: the first-choice card selected-stock-envelope matches philippeVV's fresh live CLAIM in discussions/1166 (2026-10-14 18:57Z, updates 19:21Z), so the second-choice card was taken per the collision rule. Refined to the explicit, unclaimed open handoff question 3 of PR1959 (research/t16-audit-mutant-coverage): mutation-test the frozen invoice_allcold.py. Distinct object from the released t16 template-mutant work: a different checker (the finite-invoice stage), different inputs (audit receipts, provider registry, retained invoice), and the finite inequality guards as the target predicates.
actual_scope: Mutation coverage of the selected finite invoice: one-field and fully consistent semantic mutants of invoice_allcold.run() inputs on the archived selected fixture, first-rejecting-statement census, and a downstream assemble() probe for every mutant the invoice accepts.
bottleneck_link: Closes a named acceptance-boundary question on the selected supplier chain (PR1959 open question 3): whether the invoice's finite inequalities and their inputs follow from actual rejection checks. Reliability evidence for the inherited implementation obligations; no kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop at the invoice stage's run() acceptance boundary plus one downstream admission probe (assemble()). No full cold replay, no provider-program synthesis, no kappa or supplier work.
evidence: research/invoice-mutant-coverage/EXPECTED.json: positive control reproduces the archived selected PREFIX-AND-INVOICE.json and GLOBAL-PREFIX.json exactly; 37 mutants, 31 rejected by run() at named statements, 6 accepted by run() and each rejected by assemble(); F1/F2 is an exact row-guard boundary pair (stock bit 4488 rejected, 4487 accepted by the invoice alone).

open_questions.question: Do hash-consistent provider program mutants survive the recount chain?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Class D only tests raw provider mutations, which die at the first hash mismatch. The recount bindings were never tested against an internally consistent forged program.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the harness to edit LOCAL-PROGRAMS events and resynchronize the template registry, stored hashes and LOCAL-CHECKS together.
open_questions.blocked_by: Synthesizing event edits that keep the recount identities (paid profile, real, macros, prefix bits) internally equal.

open_questions.question: Does the executed driver (verify_t16.py + indep16.py) reject the F2 stock inflation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The claim that the driver-level literals anchor the stock is a static reading of verify_t16.py; the F2 fixture only proves run() accepts and assemble() rejects.
open_questions.first_step: Run the indep16.py stage alone on the F2-mutated tree and compare rank_mass, deficit and row.
open_questions.blocked_by: The lift/bind/emit stage chain above the invoice in the strict replay.

open_questions.question: Should the retained invoice's conservative_pervertex_used be pinned at invocation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: run() accepts any positive value (class E2 is accepted downstream only by a positivity check); large values fail safe through the inequalities (class E3) but the binding is thin.
open_questions.first_step: Compare the retained invoice hash or allowance against the vendor UPSTREAM-PINS in the invoice stage.
open_questions.blocked_by: A maintainer decision on wrapping the frozen driver code.
